353 | #### Release checklist:
354 | 
355 | The [release page](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/releases) shows
356 | maintainers all merges since last release. Once we have a long enough list,
357 | we should prepare a release.
358 | 
359 | A release PR can be created by maintainers via the
360 | ["Create release pull request" GitHub Action](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/actions/workflows/create-release-pull-request.yaml). Once this is done, it's a good idea to
361 | put a short post on the #contributing channel on slack so that people know
362 | there will be a release soon.
363 | 
364 | As further PRs are merged, we may need to rerun the release script again
365 | (or alternatively just manually updating the branch). This can only be rerun
366 | locally (the GitHub Action will exit error if the branch already exists to
367 | prevent overwriting it).
368 | 
369 | Check out the release branch created by the GitHub Action locally and run
370 | the script. It will preserve any `Highlights` you have added and update the
371 | other sections with new contributions. It can be run as follows (you will
372 | need a [GitHub Personal Access Token](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/creating-a-personal-access-token) with read & write permissions on the "Content"
373 | scope, and read permissions on the "Metadata" scope. The reason we need
374 | both read & write access on the "Content" scope is that only tokens with
375 | write access can see _draft_ releases, which is what we need access to).
376 | All maintainers should have sufficient access to generate such a token. Once
377 | generated, store it in your env (zshrc, etc) as `SQLFLUFF_GITHUB_TOKEN`. Then:
378 | 
379 | ```shell
380 | make shell
381 | make release 3.4.2 # Change to your release number
382 | ```
383 | 
384 | When all of the changes planned for the release have been merged, and
385 | the release PR is up to date. The maintainer running the release should
386 | write a short commentary in the `CHANGELOG.md` file, describing any features
387 | of note, and also celebrating new contributors. Check out old releases
388 | for inspiration!
389 | 
390 | When the PR is ready. Merge it. Once merged, follow these steps to actually
391 | publish the final release.
392 | 
393 | 1. Edit the draft release on GitHub. Copy across the summary from the
394 |    `CHANGELOG.md`
395 | 2. Update the title of the release to include the current date.
